32a3e40.summary: Per-frame battle update. Tracks the pointer/target card under it, plays queued sounds, and runs the input state machine keyed on UIstate (dragging hand cards, targeted spells, attacks, active abilities). Then resolves the next queued action and handles Escape. Also handles the click-to-leave screen after the match ends.
comments: Do nothing until the battle is fully initialized
Not in a normal connected/disconnected state: only report the status change once the match is finished, then bail
Match is over and the player clicked or pressed Escape: leave the battle
Leave the Photon room if not already leaving, release card backs
Finished tutorials: go back to the main menu scene
Tutorial not finished yet: restart the scripted tutorial match against a SuperEasy AI
Convert the mouse/touch position to canvas space; mobile builds add a vertical target offset
Find the card under the pointer and remember it as the current target
No card under the pointer: hide the card description popup unless in a card-play or targeting state
Hide the deck size display once the touch is released
Play any queued sound effects
Branch on the UI state; low values are idle and hand-card states, high values are attack and targeting states
Idle state: with a finger down, tutorial scripts may suppress fading the ability description
Dragging a card from hand
Pointer released while dragging a hand card
Released too low: card is dropped back; if it could not be played, a tip is logged
Return the card to hand, restore minion layout and tell the opponent the new hand order if it changed
Still holding the card: has it been dragged above the play threshold?
Dragged above the line: check whether the card can be played
Minion goes to the playing-minion state; targeted spells to the targeted state; others to the untargeted state
Still dragging: if dragged back below the line, check if it is unplayable and return it to hand
Otherwise move the card with the pointer and make space for it in the hand
Playing a minion (placing it on the board)
Finger still down: follow the pointer, or pull the card back to hand if dragged below the line
Finger released: place the minion
In a tutorial, check that the scripted step allows playing this card in this slot, else put it back
Queue a play-card-from-hand action for the dragged minion and mark the card as waiting to be played
Spell states: targeted spell (4) and untargeted spell (5)
Untargeted spell: on release, queue the play-card action immediately
Spell card still held: follow the pointer or return it to the play area if dragged back down
Targeted spell: on release, validate the target under the pointer
Valid spell target: queue a play-card action that carries the target
No valid target: return card to hand and show the drag-to-target tip
Finger down: move the target reticle, or cancel and return to idle if pulled back down
Higher UI states: attacks, abilities, post-battle and target-choosing
Unit attacking state: only acts during the player's own turn
Released on an active-ability unit: use the ability on a valid target if actions are allowed
Otherwise try a normal attack on the target, unless the tutorial script expects something else
No valid action: cancel the attack and stop tracking
Back to idle state after finishing or cancelling
Post-battle state: click or Escape leaves the battle
Choosing a target for an ability or unit effect (by click)
Targeted active ability released: execute it if the target is valid, otherwise show a tip and cancel
Move the targeting crosshair/reticle to follow the pointer
Run the next queued action when a battle or scripted sequence is running and nothing is resolving
Escape pressed during battle: open chat/voice lines pop-up if one is available

3283338.summary: Leaves the battle: leaves the Photon room if needed, releases card backs, then loads the main menu or, if the first tutorials are not finished, starts the tutorial match again. Called when the player clicks out after a match.

Not yet leaving: warn and leave the room
Free the card back resources

32a56f8.summary: Takes the next action to resolve. Queues are checked in priority order: interrupt, instant, delayed instant, then the normal action queue. Removes the first action, marks that an action is resolving, and calls ResolveAction on it.

32a57b0.summary: Pops the first action from the given action queue and resolves it, setting the resolving flag first. Logs an error if the queue is empty.
comments: Queue has an action: mark resolving, copy it out, remove it, then resolve it
